title: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar
subject: Bail / Arrest
holding: Police officers should not automatically arrest merely because an offence is registered; liberty safeguards remain relevant.

title: Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra
subject: Anticipatory Bail
holding: Anticipatory bail protects personal liberty and requires consideration of the accusation, antecedents and flight risk.

title: Nikesh Tarachand Shah v. Union of India
subject: Economic Offences / Bail
holding: Courts should ordinarily consider bail on merits rather than impose mechanical conditions.

title: Jayahind v. State of Karnataka
subject: Regular Bail
holding: Access to justice and prompt bail consideration remain relevant during proceedings.

title: Pankaj Chahal v. State of Haryana
subject: Anticipatory Bail
holding: Cooperation with investigation and custodial necessity are relevant bail considerations.

title: Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia v. State of Punjab
subject: Anticipatory Bail
holding: Anticipatory bail powers are preventive and require conditions tailored to the facts and investigation stage.

title: Dataram Singh v. State of Uttar Pradesh
subject: Bail
holding: Bail and jail should be assessed against liberty, investigation needs and trial delay.

title: Mahmood v. State of Maharashtra
subject: Regular Bail
holding: Trial delay and continued custody may be material when assessing continued detention.

title: Neeru Yadav v. State of Uttar Pradesh
subject: Witness Protection / Bail
holding: Courts may consider a real threat to witnesses or investigation while framing bail orders.

title: State of Rajasthan v. Balchand alias Baliay
subject: Bail
holding: The basic rule is bail, not jail, except where circumstances justify custody.
